newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks end down but pare losses.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks end down but pare losses.

text.p: Mexican stocks fell Friday but recouped some ground as dealers rushed to close their books ahead of the weekend, dealers said.
"The week was closing and some dealers stepped in to defend prices at the end, so we recovered a little," said a trader.
The blue chip IPC index closed down 7.09 points, or 0.21 percent, at 3,385.13. Volume was regular at 78.9 million shares traded.
Analysts said that stocks tended to slide for most of the session due to profit-taking.
"The market continued on the slide that began yesterday, although it did respect support at 3,350 points," said Carlos Ponce, research director at the Santander financial group.

"On the other hand, as the Dow Jones is so bullish and the U.S. economy is on the right track, international investors see the U.S. markets as being less risky and are less interested in emerging markets in general," he added.
The Dow Jones industrial average rose 35.03 points to 6,348.03, its eighth straight record.
Financial stock BBVPro headed the leaders, up three centavos (one cent) at 44 (six cents) on what traders said was a technical rebound after the stock had fallen in recent sessions.
Heading the losers was truck and bus maker Dina, down 25 centavos (three cents) to 3.80 pesos (48 cents), but traders noted that this was at minimal trade.
Many blue chips closed down, notably Telmex, whose L series lost ten centavos (one cent) to 12.54 pesos ($1.59), and whose ADRs shrugged off the Dow rally to end down 37.5 cents at $31.25.
Technical analysts meanwhile said the market had been gathering a head of steam for a new rally.

"It was obvious that the bourse would show signs of fatigue when it approached record highs yesterday. We're in a consolidation period which is seeking to extend gains to 3,560 points," an analysts said.
The IPC's record close was 3,433.75 points, which it chalked up on August 27.
